clue.text: Such a volte-face could bring one to earth

parts.note: rearranging the five letters of the word heart produces the word earth, so altering that organ lands one on the ground

explanation.surface: A sudden reversal of opinion that brings someone crashing back to reality.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: change the letters of HEART and you get EARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A volte-face is a complete turnaround in opinion, and a change of feeling or mind is exactly that.

clue.text: Easily frightened like an arch-enemy

definitions.meaning: the written word arch-enemy has a hen at its heart: arc-HEN-emy

explanation.surface: Someone timid compared to a sworn foe.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: the middle of the written word 'arch-enemy' is HEN, so it has a chicken for a heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a fowl's courage is cowardly and timid, the usual sense of the idiom.

clue.text: Nurses are disheartened when she leaves

definitions.text: Nurses are disheartened when she leaves

parts.words: Nurses are disheartened when she leaves
parts.note: nurses here are ...; take away the girl's name sitting in the middle of that word and only its first and last letters are left

explanation.surface: Care staff lose heart when a colleague departs.
explanation.walkthrough: NANNIES has ANNIE at its heart, so when she goes the nannies are literally 'disheartened'.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, here hidden in the middle of the word for childminders.

clue.text: Country club for entertainers

parts.note: German describes the country of Germany
a band is a club or group of people joined together

explanation.surface: A rural club that puts on shows.
explanation.walkthrough: A German band was a troupe of street musicians, common in Victorian Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Street musicians of this kind performed for passers-by, so they are a group of performers.

clue.text: The study of chains?

parts.note: the chains are not metal links but mountain ranges, and the science of mountains is meant

explanation.surface: An academic discipline devoted to links and fetters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chains' suggests metal links; it means mountain chains.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of mountains covers mountain chains, or ranges.

clue.text: Garnishing for a pork-pie

parts.note: a pork-pie is a flat-crowned hat, so its decoration is a ribbon round the crown

explanation.surface: Something to decorate a meat pie.
explanation.walkthrough: A pork-pie is a meat pie, but also a hat with a flat round crown, named for its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon around the crown is the usual trimming on such headwear.

clue.text: Alison drops in as well

indicators.note: drops means the name lets the two letters of the following word fall out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Alison pays a visit too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops in' looks like visiting; remove I and N from ALISON.
explanation.definitionFit: Too, likewise and in addition are synonyms of this word.

clue.text: Goes round queue and makes off

parts.note: to turn is to go round, rotate
a queue is a tail, a line of people

explanation.surface: Someone circles a line of people and then leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is an idiom for running away.

clue.text: Entertainer apt to eat his own words?

definitions.text: Entertainer apt to eat his own words?

parts.words: Entertainer apt to eat his own words?
parts.note: the words are blades: the letters of 'words' are within the performer's stock-in-trade, and he gulps them down

explanation.surface: A performer who often has to retract what he says.
explanation.walkthrough: To eat one's words is to retract; here 'words' rearranges to SWORD, which he literally swallows.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground or circus performer who passes blades down his throat.

clue.text: Very private hotel nearly all occupied by king

indicators.note: occupied by means the king's letters take up residence inside the hotel phrase

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
most is nearly all of something
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: An exclusive hotel nearly full of royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepest, most secret feelings are the most private ones.

clue.text: Clever daughter deserts bad-tempered woman

indicators.note: deserts means the daughter's letter leaves the word for clever

parts.note: shrewd means clever, astute

explanation.surface: A bright daughter walks out on an irritable woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A scold or nagging woman, as in Shakespeare's Taming of the play's title.

clue.text: Many head off for animal enclosure

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, so a large number

indicators.note: off means the letters of head are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Lots of people are decapitated, in a pen for beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: A kheda is an Indian stockade for trapping wild elephants.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade used in India to capture elephants, so a pen for wild beasts.

clue.text: Ground held in no value

indicators.note: held in means the letters are kept inside the words no value

explanation.surface: A piece of land kept as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous cricket venue in Kennington, south London.

clue.text: Employer responsible for depreciation

definitions.meaning: one who employs something, puts it to use
wear and tear from use lowers an item's value

explanation.surface: A boss blamed for falling asset values.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employer' suggests a boss; it means one who employs, i.e. uses, a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone operating a machine both employs it and wears it down, causing loss of value.

clue.text: One composer having a game with another

parts.note: monte is a card game
Verdi, the Italian composer, is another one

explanation.surface: A musician plays cards with a fellow musician.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian composer of early opera, Orfeo's creator, is one such musician.

clue.text: His cries may help to stimulate the circulation?

definitions.text: His cries may help to stimulate the circulation?

parts.words: His cries may help to stimulate the circulation?
parts.note: the circulation is of a paper, not blood; a lad shouting the headlines boosts sales

explanation.surface: Someone whose shouts improve blood flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulation' suggests blood; it means a newspaper's sales.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy selling papers in the street calls out to boost readership.

clue.text: An indication of what Rudyard's Lady may draw?

definitions.text: An indication of what Rudyard's Lady may draw?

parts.words: An indication of what Rudyard's Lady may draw?
parts.note: Kipling's poem calls a liner a lady; to draw is to sink to a depth in the sea, shown by a mark on the hull

explanation.surface: A sign of what Kipling's heroine might sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudyard Kipling wrote 'The Liner She's a Lady'; a ship draws a certain depth of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The level on a ship's hull shows how deep it sits, its draught.

clue.text: Throw out almost dead rose trees

indicators.note: throw out means the letters are tossed into a new order
almost means the phrase loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Discard nearly withered roses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims DEAD ROSE to DEADROS, which 'Throw out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Himalayan cedars, a kind of large conifer.

clue.text: English — ten out of ten perhaps by agreement

indicators.note: out means the first ten is jumbled
perhaps means the second ten is shuffled too

explanation.surface: An English pupil scores full marks, agreed by all.
explanation.walkthrough: Each TEN is rearranged to NTE, giving E + NTE + NTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: Describes something that has happened before

definitions.text: Describes something that has happened before

parts.words: Describes something that has happened before
parts.note: a word for what took place at a previous time

explanation.surface: A word for past events.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that occurred previously happened at a prior time.

clue.text: Paterson's song and dance girl?

parts.note: Banjo Paterson wrote the Australian song about waltzing a girl's name, the dance being a waltz

explanation.surface: A showgirl in Paterson's musical.
explanation.walkthrough: Banjo Paterson was the Australian poet who wrote 'Waltzing Matilda'; she is the girl who waltzes.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl's name in Australia's unofficial anthem, who goes waltzing.

clue.text: Intoxicating mixture here pound a carton

parts.note: to mash is to pound, crush
a tub is a carton or container

explanation.surface: A heady brew: crush a box.
explanation.walkthrough: In brewing, the mash is soaked in a mash tub before becoming beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The vessel where malt is steeped is where the boozy mixture is made.

clue.text: Exceptional combination of forces

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: An outstanding joint military operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Unusual and uncommon things are scarce.

clue.text: Cutter to alter a short skirt

indicators.note: to alter means the letters are changed around
short means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A tailor shortens a skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims SKIRT to SKIR, which 'to alter' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malay dagger with a wavy blade.

clue.text: Liable to receive a backhander?

parts.note: a backhander is not a slap but a bribe, and someone open to bribery is meant

explanation.surface: Someone likely to be slapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backhander' suggests a blow; it is slang for a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt and open to bribery.

clue.text: New advertisement about excellent spirit

parts.note: AI is A1, first-class

explanation.surface: A new advert about a fine drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A water nymph in classical myth.

clue.text: Pointless cutting instrument

indicators.note: pointless means a compass point, S for south, is taken away

parts.note: sharp means cutting, keen-edged

explanation.surface: A blunt cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument plucked by hand.

clue.text: Little by little chap picks up a girl

parts.note: Eric is the hero of Farrar's novel Eric, or Little by Little

explanation.surface: A man gradually picks up a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eric, or Little by Little' is a Victorian school story by F. W. Farrar.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female forename, also the botanical name for heather, so a fair example of a girl.

clue.text: Struggle in winter perhaps to get an audience

indicators.note: in means the struggle word goes inside the jumbled season
perhaps means the letters of winter are rearranged

parts.note: to vie is to struggle, compete

explanation.surface: A fight in the cold season to gain a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggle' looks like the definition, but it is the inserted piece; the definition is 'audience', in its sense of a formal hearing with someone important.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal meeting with an important person.

clue.text: Theatre producer, exponent of power play

parts.note: the Empire is a typical name for a theatre
a builder is a producer, a maker

explanation.surface: A stage impresario who loves power games.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who seeks to extend their influence and control.
